outcome: morbidity associated with CPAP (CPAP belly, nasal crusting, IVH, BPD, PDA, ROP)
cohort: 100 preterm neonates <34 weeks with mild to moderate respiratory distress (Silverman Anderson score 3-5), excluding those with congenital heart disease, congenital anomalies, requiring mechanical ventilation at birth, Silverman Anderson score > 6, severe birth asphyxia, shock, or apnea; 50 neonates received early CPAP (group 1) and 50 neonates received delayed CPAP (historical controls, group 2).
finding: Early initiation of CPAP at birth was associated with reduced need for intubation, surfactant therapy, and mechanical ventilation, as well as lower morbidity and mortality.
birth_weight: Not specified, but no significant difference between groups
